- When sentiment is positive (≥0.2) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.  
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., +5%+ in 3–5 days), model often overshoots; cap forecast at 10–15% above recent peak.  
- If sentiment is neutral or negative (≤0.0), model underestimates; add 1–2% to forecast to account for mean reversion bias.  
- Model consistently underestimates in early forecast horizon (e.g., 1–3 days ahead) — adjust downward by 0.5–1.5% for short-term.  
- If recent 3–5 day average is rising, model overreacts; apply smoothing filter to reduce volatility in forecast.  
- When sentiment history shows repeated 0.00 values, model exhibits lag — delay forecast adjustment by 1–2 days.
